questions.explanation:
Equation of line joining $\left(1,2,3\right)$ and $\left(2,3,4\right)$ is

$\vec{r} = \left(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\right) + \lambda \left(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}\right)$

${\vec{b}}_{1} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k} {\vec{b}}_{2} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 0\hat{k}$

${\vec{b}}_{1} \times {\vec{b}}_{2} = \left( \begin{matrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & - 1 & 0\end{matrix} \right) = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k} \implies \left({\vec{b}}_{1} \times {\vec{b}}_{2}\right) = \sqrt{14}$

questions.question: The vertices $B$ and $C$ of a $\Delta ABC$ lie on the line, $\frac{x + 2}{3} = \frac{y - 1}{0} = \frac{z}{4}$ such that $BC = 5$ units. Then the area (in sq. units) of this triangle, given the point $A\left(1,\text{ } - 1,\text{ }2\right),$ is
questions.explanation: The points $B$ and $C$ lie on the line $\frac{x + 2}{3} = \frac{y - 1}{0} = \frac{z}{4}.$ Draw perpendicular $AD$ on the line $BC.$ Clearly area of $\Delta ABC = \frac{1}{2}⋅AD⋅BC$ To find a point on the line, let $\frac{x + 2}{3} = \frac{y - 1}{0} = \frac{z}{4} = r \implies x + 2 = 3r,y - 1 = 0,z = 4r \implies x = 3r - 2,y = 1,z = 4r$ Thus, the point $D \equiv \left(3r - 2,1,4r\right)$ The direction ratios of a line joining two points $\left({x}_{1},{y}_{1},{z}_{1}\right)$ and $\left({x}_{2},{y}_{2},{z}_{2}\right)$ are $< {x}_{2} - {x}_{1},{y}_{2} - {y}_{1},{z}_{2} - {z}_{1} >$ Thus, the direction ratios of $AD$ are $< 3r - 2 - 1,1 + 1,4r - 2 > = < 3r - 3,2,4r - 2 >$ Since $AD$ is perpendicular to given line, hence the dot product of their direction ratios is zero. $\implies 3 \cdot \left(3r - 3\right) + 0 \cdot 2 + 4 \cdot \left(4r - 2\right) = 0 \implies 9r - 9 + 16r - 8 = 0 \implies 25r - 17 = 0 \implies r = \frac{17}{25} \implies D \equiv \left(3 \times \frac{17}{25} - 2,1,4 \times \frac{17}{25}\right) = \left(\frac{1}{25},1,\frac{68}{25}\right)$ The distance between the points $\left({x}_{1},{y}_{1},{z}_{1}\right) & \left({x}_{2},{y}_{2},{z}_{2}\right)$ is $\sqrt{{\left({x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left({y}_{1} - {y}_{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left({z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right)}^{2}} \implies AD = \sqrt{{\left(\frac{1}{25} - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(1 + 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(\frac{68}{25} - 2\right)}^{2}} \implies AD = \sqrt{\frac{576}{625} + 4 + \frac{324}{625}} \implies AD = \sqrt{\frac{136}{25}} \implies AD = \frac{2}{5}\sqrt{34}$ units Hence, the area of $\Delta ABC = \frac{1}{2}⋅\left(\frac{2}{5}\sqrt{34}\right)⋅5 = \sqrt{34}$ sq units. `

Now again,

S.D. $= \frac{\left(\left(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}\right) \cdot \left(\left(15 - 4\lambda \right)\hat{i} + \left(\lambda - 10\right)\hat{j} + 5k\right)\right)}{\sqrt{{\left(15 - 4\lambda \right)}^{2} + {\left(\lambda - 10\right)}^{2} + 25}} \frac{\left(15 - 4\lambda + 2\lambda - 20 + 10\right)}{\sqrt{{\left(15 - 4\lambda \right)}^{2} + {\left(\lambda - 10\right)}^{2} + 25}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

squaring both side we get,

questions.question: The shortest distance between the lines $\frac{x - 2}{3} = \frac{y + 1}{2} = \frac{z - 6}{2}$ and $\frac{x - 6}{3} = \frac{1 - y}{2} = \frac{z + 8}{0}$ is equal to ______
questions.explanation:
Given equations are

$\frac{x - 2}{3} = \frac{y + 1}{2} = \frac{z - 6}{2}$ is passing through a point $\left(2, - 1,6\right)$ and it's direction ratios are $3,2,2$.

So,

${\vec{a}}_{1} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 6\hat{k} {\vec{b}}_{1} = 3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$

And,

$\frac{x - 6}{3} = \frac{y - 1}{ - 2} = \frac{z + 8}{0}$ is passing through a point $\left(6,1, - 8\right)$ and it's direction ratios are $3, - 2,0$.

${\vec{a}}_{2} = 6\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 8\hat{k} {\vec{b}}_{2} = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 0\hat{k}$

Now,

${\vec{a}}_{2} - {\vec{a}}_{1} = 4\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 14\hat{k} {\vec{b}}_{1} \times {\vec{b}}_{2} = \left( \begin{matrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & - 2 & 0\end{matrix} \right) \implies {\vec{b}}_{1} \times {\vec{b}}_{2} = 4\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} - 12\hat{k}$

So,

$\implies \left({\vec{b}}_{1} \times {\vec{b}}_{2}\right) = \sqrt{16 + 36 + 144} = 14$

We know that the shortest distance between two skew lines is $\frac{\left(\left({\vec{a}}_{2} - {\vec{a}}_{1}\right) \cdot \left({\vec{b}}_{1} \times {\vec{b}}_{2}\right)\right)}{\left({\vec{b}}_{1} \times {\vec{b}}_{2}\right)} = \left(\frac{\left(4\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 14\hat{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} - 12\hat{k}\right)}{14}\right) = \frac{\left(16 + 12 + 168\right)}{14} = 14$ units

questions.question: The line of shortest distance between the lines $\frac{x - 2}{0} = \frac{y - 1}{1} = \frac{z}{1}$ and $\frac{x - 3}{2} = \frac{y - 5}{2} = \frac{z - 1}{1}$ makes an angle of ${\sin }^{ - 1}\left(\sqrt{\frac{2}{27}}\right)$ with the plane $P : ax - y - z = 0,\left(a > 0\right)$. If the image of the point $\left(1,1, - 5\right)$ in the plane $P$ is $\left(\alpha ,\beta ,\gamma \right)$, then $\alpha + \beta - \gamma$ is equal to _____ .
questions.explanation:
Given lines, $\frac{x - 2}{0} = \frac{y - 1}{1} = \frac{z}{1}$ and $\frac{x - 3}{2} = \frac{y - 5}{2} = \frac{z - 1}{1}$

Now direction ratio of line of shortest distance will be,

$\left( \begin{matrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 1\end{matrix} \right) = - \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$

Now given angle between line and plane is ${\sin }^{ - 1}\sqrt{\frac{2}{27}} = \alpha$, so $\sin \alpha = \sqrt{\frac{2}{27}}$

Now direction ratio of normal to plane is $\left(a, - 1, - 1\right)$

So, $\sin \alpha = \left(\frac{ - a - 2 + 2}{\sqrt{4 + 4 + 1}\sqrt{{a}^{2} + 1 + 1}}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3\sqrt{3}} \implies \sqrt{3}\left(a\right) = \sqrt{2}\sqrt{{a}^{2} + 2} \implies 3{a}^{2} = 2{a}^{2} + 4 \implies {a}^{2} = 4 \implies a = 2\left(\text{as}a > 0\text{given}\right)$

Now equation of plane will be $2x - y - z = 0$ and image of point $\left(1,1, - 5\right)$ will be,

$\frac{x - 1}{2} = \frac{y - 1}{ - 1} = \frac{z + 5}{ - 1} = - 2\frac{\left(2 - 1 + 5\right)}{{2}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}} \implies \frac{x - 1}{2} = \frac{y - 1}{ - 1} = \frac{z + 5}{ - 1} = - 2 \implies x = - 3,y = 3,z = - 3$

So, $\alpha = - 3,\beta = 3,\gamma = - 3$

So, $\alpha + \beta - \gamma = - 3 + 3 + 3 = 3$

questions.question: If the shortest distance between the lines $\vec{{r}_{1}} = \alpha \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k} + \lambda \left(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}\right),\lambda \in R,\alpha > 0$ and $\vec{{r}_{2}} = - 4\hat{i} - \hat{k} + \mu \left(3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}\right),\mu \in R$ is $9,$ then $\alpha$ is equal to_____.
questions.explanation:
We have,

$\vec{{r}_{1}} = \alpha \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k} + \lambda \left(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}\right) \vec{{r}_{2}} = - 4\hat{i} - \hat{k} + \mu \left(3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}\right)$

If $\vec{r} = \vec{a} + \lambda \vec{b}$ and $\vec{r} = \vec{c} + \lambda \vec{d}$, then shortest distance between two lines is

$L = \frac{\left(\vec{a} - \vec{c}\right) \cdot \left(\vec{b} \times \vec{d}\right)}{\left(\vec{b} \times \vec{d}\right)}$

Here,

$\vec{b} \times \vec{d} = \left( \begin{matrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & - 2 & 2 \\ 3 & - 2 & - 2\end{matrix} \right) \implies \vec{b} \times \vec{d} = 8\hat{i} + 8\hat{j} + 4\hat{k} \implies \vec{b} \times \vec{d} = 4\left(2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}\right) \implies \left(\vec{b} \times \vec{d}\right) = 4 \cdot 3$

And,

$\vec{a} - \vec{c} = \left(\left(\alpha + 4\right)\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\right)$

So, shortest distance is

$\frac{\left(\left(\alpha + 4\right)\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\right) \cdot 4\left(2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}\right)}{4 \cdot 3} = 9 \implies 2\left(\alpha + 4\right) + 4 + 3 = 27 \implies \left(\alpha + 4\right) = 10 \implies \alpha = 6$

questions.question: If the lines $\frac{x - 1}{2} = \frac{2 - y}{ - 3} = \frac{z - 3}{\alpha }$ and $\frac{x - 4}{5} = \frac{y - 1}{2} = \frac{z}{\beta }$ intersect, then the magnitude of the minimum value of $8\alpha \beta$ is _____.
questions.explanation:
Let,

${L}_{1} = \frac{x - 1}{2} = \frac{y - 2}{3} = \frac{z - 3}{\alpha } = \lambda {L}_{2} = \frac{x - 4}{5} = \frac{y - 1}{2} = \frac{z - 0}{\beta } = \mu$

For point of intersection

$2\lambda + 1 = 5\mu + 4...\left(i\right) 3\lambda + 2 = 2\mu + 1...\left(\mathrm{ii}\right) \alpha \lambda + 3 = \beta \mu + 0...\left(\mathrm{iii}\right)$

From $\left(i\right)$ and $\left(\mathrm{ii}\right)$, we get $\lambda = \mu = - 1$

Now, from $\left(\mathrm{iii}\right)$, we get $\alpha - \beta = 3$

Let $y = 8\alpha \beta \implies y = 8\alpha \left(\alpha - 3\right) \implies y = 8\left({\alpha }^{2} - 3\alpha + \frac{9}{4}\right) - 18 \implies y = 8{\left(\alpha - \frac{3}{2}\right)}^{2} - 18$

So, Minimum value of $y = - 18$ at $\alpha = + \frac{3}{2}$

questions.question: Let $O$ be the origin, and $M$ and $N$ be the points on the lines $\frac{x - 5}{4} = \frac{y - 4}{1} = \frac{z - 5}{3}$ and $\frac{x + 8}{12} = \frac{y + 2}{5} = \frac{z + 11}{9}$ respectively such that $MN$ is the shortest distance between the given lines. Then $\vec{OM} \cdot \vec{ON}$ is equal to _________.
questions.explanation:
Let,

${L}_{1} : \frac{x - 5}{4} = \frac{y - 4}{1} = \frac{z - 5}{3} = \lambda \implies M(4\lambda + 5,\lambda + 4,3\lambda + 5)$

And ${L}_{2} : \frac{x + 8}{12} = \frac{y + 2}{5} = \frac{z + 11}{9} = \mu \implies N(12\mu - 8,5\mu - 2,9\mu - 11)$

Now, finding $\vec{MN} = (4\lambda - 12\mu + 13,\lambda - 5\mu + 6,3\lambda - 9\mu + 16).. \dots \left(1\right)$

Now finding cross product of direction ratios of line we get,

${\vec{b}}_{1} \times {\vec{b}}_{2} = \left( \begin{matrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 4 & 1 & 3 \\ 12 & 5 & 9\end{matrix} \right) = - 6\hat{i} + 8\hat{k} \dots ...\left(2\right)$

Now, solving the equation $\left(1\right) & \left(2\right)$ as they are parallel vectors, we get,

$∴\frac{4\lambda - 12\mu + 13}{ - 6} = \frac{\lambda - 5\mu + 6}{0} = \frac{3\lambda - 9\mu + 16}{8}$

Taking $\frac{4\lambda - 12\mu + 13}{ - 6} = \frac{\lambda - 5\mu + 6}{0} \implies \lambda - 5\mu + 6 = 0 \dots \left(3\right)$

Taking $\frac{4\lambda - 12\mu + 13}{ - 6} = \frac{3\lambda - 9\mu + 16}{8} \lambda - 3\mu + 4 = 0 \dots \left(4\right)$

Solve $\left(3\right)$ and $\left(4\right)$ we get

$\lambda = - 1,\mu = 1$

So, $M(1,3,2)$ and $N(4,3, - 2)$

Hence, $\vec{OM} \cdot \vec{ON} = 4 + 9 - 4 = 9$

questions.question: Let $O$ be the origin and the position vector of $A$ and $B$ be $2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$ respectively. If the internal bisector of $∠AOB$ meets the line $AB$ at $C$, then the length of $OC$ is
